decision: Do not expand unchanged unit-feedback to bank1 and do not sweep feedback weights. It reduces the selected bank2 reverse failure but does not provide a stable strong-baseline gain. Next inspect actual calibration corrections as a candidate memory target, rather than append whole calibrated-model states.
evidence: Versus bilateral: bank0+0.2100/+0.2781pp, bank2-0.0265/-0.3876pp. Four-case mean+0.0185pp. Bank2 reverse single-task deletion remains negative. Versus the prior count-weighted candidate the four-case mean is+0.1466pp, mostly a rescue of its worst case.
mechanism_limits: Retained memory energy falls from roughly23k to roughly4k, but stable baseline gains do not follow. Removing feedback mass growth is insufficient. This does not prove a unique cause of failure or that supervised correction memory will work.
next_action: Read-only parameter-geometry diagnostic using frozen native stage checkpoints; no new training or held-out evaluation. Quantify calibration correction relative to initial convex merge and its component outside the old/new row span before specifying the next concrete operator.
